summary: As of Thursday, September 24, before the U.S. open, the Nasdaq setup is slightly negative but highly event-dependent. Wednesday's session ended with the Nasdaq Composite down about 1.1% after Treasury yields surged, with the 10-year moving above 5.1% to its highest level since 2007 as stronger-than-expected U.S. business activity and firmer oil revived inflation concerns. That is the clearest near-term counterweight for long-duration technology shares after the Nasdaq had reached record highs earlier in the week.

The supportive side is that AI and semiconductor leadership has remained structurally strong, while today's Trump-Xi meeting creates meaningful upside optionality if the two sides signal trade stabilization, selective tariff relief, or constructive cooperation around AI. The problem for the pre-market setup is that rates and oil have reasserted themselves at the same time that the index is coming off record territory. With the U.S.-China summit, Middle East diplomacy, labor data and several Fed speakers all capable of moving yields or risk appetite, today's direction is likely to depend more on incoming headlines than on Wednesday's close alone.

events.title: 1. Trump-Xi summit in Washington — timing of market-moving headlines uncertain
events.detail: President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping meet today, with trade, tariffs, AI, critical minerals and Taiwan among the key issues surrounding the visit. Markets have been leaning toward stabilization rather than a comprehensive agreement, so even targeted tariff relief or a constructive extension of the trade truce could support semiconductors and other China-sensitive technology shares. Conversely, tougher language on export controls, Taiwan or strategic technology could quickly pressure Nasdaq leadership. Because headlines can emerge throughout the visit, this is the day's largest event-risk wildcard rather than a single scheduled data release.

events.title: 2. Initial jobless claims — 8:30 ET
events.detail: Weekly initial claims are expected around 201,000 versus 196,000 previously. After Wednesday's jump in Treasury yields, the market is especially sensitive to evidence that the labor market remains too firm for inflation and rate pressures to ease. A modestly softer reading could help yields retreat and support growth stocks; a notably stronger labor signal could reinforce the higher-for-longer rates pressure on Nasdaq valuations.

events.title: 3. Fed speakers — early morning through the U.S. session
events.detail: New York Fed President John Williams is scheduled around 4:10 ET, with Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin around 8:00-8:30 ET and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack around 8:50 ET; Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson is scheduled around 10:10 ET. Following last week's Fed rate increase and Wednesday's renewed yield spike, any comments on inflation persistence, further tightening or the tolerance for high long-term yields can matter disproportionately for technology multiples.

events.title: 4. Middle East and oil headlines — ongoing
events.detail: Markets continue to monitor efforts to reduce Middle East tensions after oil moved higher again Wednesday. The Nasdaq implication is largely through inflation expectations and Treasury yields: credible diplomatic progress that pulls crude lower would remove an important macro headwind, while renewed escalation or another oil spike could push yields higher and intensify pressure on long-duration technology shares.

events.title: 5. Costco earnings — after the close
events.detail: Costco reports fiscal fourth-quarter results after today's cash session. It is not a core semiconductor catalyst, but as a very large Nasdaq-100 consumer name its results and commentary on demand, pricing and costs can provide a useful read on the U.S. consumer and inflation backdrop. The report is more relevant to the post-close and Friday setup than to today's opening direction.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the first question is whether Wednesday's bond selloff extends or stabilizes. If the 10-year yield backs away from the 5.1% area, oil cools and Trump-Xi headlines lean constructive, the combination could allow semiconductors and mega-cap technology to regain leadership and turn the setup more positive. If yields remain above 5% and push higher while oil stays firm, even constructive China headlines may struggle to overcome valuation pressure; a negative surprise from the summit or renewed Middle East escalation on top of high yields would create the clearest downside scenario. Breadth and semiconductor relative strength should help distinguish a durable rebound from a narrow relief bounce.
keyTimes: The U.S. cash market opens at 9:30 ET, which is 16:30 in Istanbul. The most important scheduled pre-open window is 8:30 ET (15:30 Istanbul) for initial jobless claims and associated rate reaction, with Fed commentary clustered around the morning and Paulson around 10:10 ET (17:10 Istanbul). Trump-Xi and Middle East headlines can arrive at any time and may ultimately be more important than the scheduled releases.
